item.content:encoded:
Hey, neat James Taylor reference.

In all honesty, I'm not really sure how to react to this tale. I appreciate the courage to approach this subject matter so sensitively, and it's not like there's any overtly offensive content here. But I feel like the tale just… goes past a little too quickly for my tastes? This doesn't delve into the topic of self-harm as deeply as I think it could go, and at the end I felt there was a lot to be desired. How Bright's immortality and tendency to self-harm can interact with one another is definitely grounds for an interesting story, and I think you captured some of that here, but as for right now, I feel that wasn't explored to a full-enough extent.

For the time being, I'm going to novote, but this definitely feels like a tale that will grow on me in the future, so I might leave an upvote later on.
